checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the KZG batch verification equation correctly implemented and resistant to invalid proof acceptance?

reachability.notes: Attacker sends crafted data column sidecars. The verification equation is the final cryptographic gate. If the random challenge r has insufficient entropy or the equation is incorrectly implemented, invalid proofs could pass.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) and identify the pairing computation: e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]). 2. Verify that LL = g1_lincomb(proofs, r_powers) is computed correctly using all provided proofs. 3. Verify LR correctly references KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n] with proper index bounds. 4. Verify RL = RLC - RLI + RLP computation is correct (no off-by-one, no overflow). 5. Test with deliberately malformed proofs: ensure they are rejected. 6. Test with valid proofs: ensure they pass. 7. Verify random challenge r has sufficient entropy (at least 128 bits from secure source). 8. Check for edge cases: empty batch, single element batch, maximum size batch. 9. Verify that the probability of accepting invalid proofs is bounded by 1/p.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Source Invariant: SG-015:INV-001, Trust Boundary: tb-002. This is a CRITICAL boundary check - the verification equation is the final cryptographic gate protecting data availability guarantees.

checklist.title: Verify Random Challenge Generation: Does the batch verifier use cryptographically secure randomness for the Fiat-Shamir challenge?

reachability.notes: Weak randomness in the challenge r could allow an attacker to craft proofs that satisfy the verification equation despite being invalid.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the source of randomness for r_powers computation in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl. 2. Verify the challenge r is derived via Fiat-Shamir transform including all relevant inputs (commitments, cells, proofs, indices). 3. Check that the hash function used is cryptographically secure (e.g., SHA-256, BLAKE2). 4. Verify no attacker-controllable inputs are excluded from the challenge computation. 5. Test if the challenge generation is deterministic given the same inputs (required for consensus). 6. Verify the challenge is in the correct field (scalar field of the curve).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Supporting check for main invariant. Insufficient entropy in the random challenge r is explicitly called out in the property notes as a potential attack vector.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Input Validation: Are data column sidecars properly validated before reaching the batch verifier?

reachability.notes: The validation layers (P2P gossip validation, Length checks, Range checks) must be correctly implemented to prevent malformed data from reaching the batch verifier.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the data flow from P2P message receipt to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl. 2. Verify P2P gossip validation rejects messages from non-subscribed topics. 3. Verify length checks: cell data has correct size, proof arrays match expected lengths. 4. Verify range checks: column indices are within valid range, row indices are valid. 5. Test with oversized/undersized inputs at each validation layer. 6. Test with out-of-range indices. 7. Verify validation failures result in message rejection (not processing with default values).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Supporting boundary check for actors: actor-p2p-peer, actor-validator-node. These nodes are covered by the property and represent the entry points for attacker-controlled data.
